item.title: Four hundred words about nothing in particular
item.dc:creator: ipsum
item.content:encoded:
There is a particular pleasure in writing that has no assignment. No brief, no keyword, no point to land — just the sound of sentences agreeing with each other down a quiet column.

This post exists for exactly that. It is here so you can watch a paragraph breathe: the measure comfortable, the links dotted and unhurried, the margins minding their own business. If you are reading this on a phone, the column has already made its adjustments without mentioning them.

Somewhere around the second paragraph of a post like this, a reader decides whether the page is a pleasant place to be. Nothing decides that faster than type. Not the header, not the colors — the type, doing its steady work line after line.

So consider this a test drive with no destination. Four hundred words, give or take, about nothing in particular — which was, of course, the subject all along.
item.excerpt:encoded: A test drive with no destination — four hundred words about the pleasure of a quiet column.

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: I came here for nothing in particular and found exactly that. Lovely.
That's the nicest thing anyone has said about a post with no subject.
Don't let it go to your head. Or do. It has plenty of room.
Four comments deep and still on topic, which is to say no topic at all.

Two things.
First, the column really does make its adjustments on a phone. I checked, standing in a queue.
Second, I would happily read four hundred more words about nothing. Take your time.

item.title: Something to hear while you type
item.dc:creator: ipsum
item.content:encoded:
Writing has a soundtrack, even when it’s just the keyboard.

The player above dresses for the occasion—light controls on light pages, dark on dark. Small manners like that are what a theme is most of the time.
item.excerpt:encoded: On keyboards, soundtracks, and a player with good manners.

item.title: Pictures until the pictures arrive
item.dc:creator: ipsum
item.content:encoded:
Photographs are placeholders too, in their way—each one standing in for the hour it was taken.

The two below wear the theme's own ink. Change the style variation and they change with it: same pictures, different light. Try it in the Styles panel and watch the whole page agree with itself.

No caption could compete with that trick, so this one won't try.

item.title: The elements of a post
item.dc:creator: ipsum
item.content:encoded:
Every post is a small collection of furniture. Here is the full set, arranged for inspection.

Words about words

And when your own words run out, you borrow better ones:

The quotation stands on its own small stage, waiting for someone worth quoting.

The Editor

Things in rows

Some content prefers a grid. The table below seats each element next to its job and its general mood:

Lists are the table's casual cousins — the same instinct for order, none of the borders:

  • Bullets in the margin's own color
  • Numbers in a matching mood
  • Nothing louder than the text

Filed, not forgotten

Nothing dramatic. That's rather the charm of an accordion: it keeps the page quiet until you ask.

More of the same, which is exactly what you hoped. An accordion with a single drawer is just a box.

For the technically inclined

Most of the details above come down to one small rule apiece. This is the one that draws the dotted underlines:

a, u, ins {
  text-decoration-style: dotted;
  text-decoration-thickness: 1px;
  text-underline-offset: 0.1em;
}

That’s the whole set. Everything else is just writing.
item.excerpt:encoded: Headings, quotes, tables, lists, an accordion, and a little code—the full furniture set, arranged for inspection.

item.title: About

item.content:encoded: Ipsum is a placeholder that stopped waiting. This site exists to show what a blank canvas looks like the moment someone starts writing on it—which is to say, it exists for the same reason any blog does.

item.title: This is a post without a featured image, and a title that takes two or three lines
item.dc:creator: ipsum
item.content:encoded:
Some posts show up with nothing but words. No image to lean on, no visual to set the mood—just a headline and whatever follows it.

There's a word for text that holds a page while it waits to become something: placeholder. This one decided to skip the waiting and just be the something.

Which is the point, really. If a layout only works once the pictures arrive, it was never much of a layout.
item.excerpt:encoded: No image, long title, nothing to hide behind—and the layout holds anyway.

item.title: This is a post with a featured image
item.dc:creator: ipsum
item.content:encoded:
A picture is worth a thousand words, which is convenient—this post only packed about seventy.

With the image doing the heavy lifting up top, the text gets to relax: two unhurried paragraphs, a comfortable measure, and nowhere in particular to be.

A picture is worth a thousand words, but somebody still has to write the caption.

Someone at the picture desk

The editor asked if it needed anything more. It did not. It stopped being a placeholder the moment you read it.
item.excerpt:encoded: Seventy words, one photograph, and a fair division of labor between them.

item.title: Patterns
item.dc:creator: ipsum
item.content:encoded:
Patterns are the theme's ready-made arrangements: insert one, then make it yours. Every pattern below is pulled live from the theme's own files through a Pattern block, so this page always shows them as they are today. Open it in the editor and each one turns back into ordinary blocks—save it from there and it stops following the files.

About

ipsum/about-row

Banners

Openers for the top of a page. Both also work as a header.

ipsum/hero-colophon

ipsum/hero-epigraph

Call to action

ipsum/cta-membership

ipsum/cta-search

Contact

ipsum/contact-say-hi

Gallery

The same pictures, three widths and two arrangements.

ipsum/gallery-grid

ipsum/gallery-grid-wide

ipsum/gallery-grid-full

ipsum/gallery-offset

ipsum/gallery-offset-full

Posts

A section lead with the latest posts, and two post bodies for links and recordings. The posts “Elsewhere: where lorem ipsum comes from” and “Dreamland, on repeat” are built from those two.

ipsum/archive-lead

ipsum/format-link

ipsum/format-audio

The other post lists (ipsum/archive-columns, ipsum/archive-compact, ipsum/archive-full, ipsum/archive-minimal, ipsum/archive-photographic, ipsum/archive-simple and ipsum/archive-standard) follow whatever list the template hands them. On a page that list is the page itself, so they live in templates instead. The category and tag pages use ipsum/archive-compact, and the home page shows the latest posts in full. To try another one, select the post list in a template in the Site Editor and choose a different design for it.

Testimonials

ipsum/kind-words

Text

ipsum/events-list

ipsum/text-alternating

ipsum/text-faqs

ipsum/text-statement

ipsum/text-statement-wide

Pages

Whole-page layouts, offered when you start a new page. They want a page to themselves, so each one has its own, on the Pages No Title template: Bio (ipsum/page-bio), Coming soon (ipsum/page-soon) and Blog home (ipsum/page-blog-home).

Headers, footers and menus

These are made for template parts, not for pages: inside a page they would add a second site title and menu, the sticky ones would follow you down the screen, and the menu overlays only close from inside a menu. So you'll find them around the content instead. Every page here wears ipsum/header-default and ipsum/footer, and the menu button on a small screen opens ipsum/navigation-overlay. The sidebar templates, on the Colophon page for one, close with ipsum/footer-wide.

The rest are a swap away in the Site Editor: replace the header with ipsum/header-collapsed, ipsum/header-sticky or ipsum/header-vertical, the footer with ipsum/footer-centered, ipsum/footer-social or ipsum/footer-subscribe, and the menu overlay with ipsum/overlay-contents or ipsum/overlay-profile.

item.title: Block styles
item.dc:creator: ipsum
item.content:encoded:
A block style is a second outfit for a block: same content, different clothes. Select a block and pick one from its Styles panel. Here is every style Ipsum offers, each worn by a few plain words, with the class name it adds underneath.

Headings and paragraphs

Three styles, shared by both. The first is for saying one thing loudly.

A heading in Display

And a paragraph that thinks it is one.

Display · is-style-text-display

The second hangs a quotation mark over a line worth repeating.

Write the sentence first. The page can wait.

Quote Mark · is-style-text-quote-mark

The third is the same mark for a card in a strong color: it takes the color of the text instead of a faint line.

The page can wait. It always has.

Quote Mark on Color · is-style-text-quote-mark-on-color

Display also fits the Site Title, the Post Title and, on archive pages, the Query Title. Here are the first two, showing this site's name and this page's:

Group

Crop Contents trims whatever spills past the edges of a group, so a word can run off the card on purpose.

Ipsum

The word above is cut off by the card, not by accident.

Crop Contents · is-style-crop-contents

Code

Evening keeps code on a dark slab, whatever the style variation. Fittingly, this is the whole of Crop Contents:

.is-style-crop-contents {
  overflow: clip;
}

Evening · is-style-evening

Buttons

Fill for the thing you hope people click, Outline for the thing they might click instead.

item.title: Colophon
item.dc:creator: ipsum
item.content:encoded:
This site runs on Ipsum, a theme named after the placeholder text that fills a page until the real words arrive. Everything here is there to show what it can do, which is mostly to stay out of the way of the writing.

Type

The reading text is Inter. Dates, categories and other small print are Manrope, a little bolder, and code is JetBrains Mono. The typography presets in the Styles panel trade them for other families in one click.

Color

Six colors do all the work: a background, the text, an accent, a faint line, a faint surface and the strongest text. Each style variation redefines all six at once, so the whole site changes together, pictures included.

This page

This page uses the Pages Sidebar template, so it shares the screen with the categories and the most recent posts. Posts have a sidebar template too: “The weather, for the record” and “Something to hear while you type” wear it. For pages made entirely of patterns there is Pages No Title, which the pages under Patterns use.

Where to look

  • Patterns shows every pattern the theme offers, grouped the way the inserter groups them.
  • Block styles shows every block style, from Display headings to Sharp logos.
  • “The elements of a post” and “The rest of the furniture” lay out the blocks a post is made of.
  • The Essays, Pictures and Sounds categories show the archive template, and the search bar at the bottom of the screen shows the search one.

item.title: The rest of the furniture
item.dc:creator: ipsum
item.content:encoded:
“The elements of a post” laid out the everyday furniture. These are the pieces that come out on special occasions.

Said twice, on purpose

A pullquote repeats something the page has already said, only louder, for the reader who skims.

Lines that keep their breaks

Lorem ipsum, said the page,
to no one in particular.
Dolor sit amet, it went on,
and waited for the words.

Spaces, kept

Draft one     too long
Draft two     too short
Draft three   fine, actually

Tucked away

Where does lorem ipsum come from?

From Cicero, more or less. It is a scrambled passage of his writing on pleasure and pain, cut off mid-word: dolorem ipsum lost its first syllable and became lorem ipsum.

Does anyone read the rest of it?

Almost nobody, which is rather the point.

One thing at a time

Coffee, a blank page, and the optimism of someone who hasn't started yet.

Second paragraphs, second coffee, and a sudden interest in tidying the desk.

The draft is finished, or at least it has stopped arguing.

Wider than the words

The column stays narrow for reading, but a picture can step out to the wide width when it has something to show.

Things that usually live in a sidebar

The latest posts, the latest comments, the categories and a calendar. They are just as happy in the middle of a post.

That's the rest of the set. The room is fully furnished; now it needs someone to sit down and write.
item.excerpt:encoded: Pullquotes, verse, tabs, a drawer or two and the things that usually live in a sidebar—the rest of the furniture set.
